author: Tulane Public Relations
why: A student at a studio desk cutting and assembling a balsa-and-card architectural model, with finished site models in the foreground: the design studio itself, not a building.
cropNote: Centre crop keeps her hands, the drawing and the model row; the upper background is a plain pale wall, so text over the lower half sits on the pale models and desk.

author: NASA Ames Research Center
why: A scale airliner model mounted on its sting in a low-speed wind tunnel test section: aerodynamics testing, exactly what the keywords name.
cropNote: Model sits in the centre band of the crop; walls and floor are pale grey and smooth, a quiet ground for text. Airline livery is a plain white model with no readable name.

author: Rhododendrites
why: A glassblower at the bench shaping a gather on the pipe, with the glory hole glowing behind: the glass studio in use.
cropNote: Centre crop holds the maker and the glowing furnace; the rest is muted grey concrete and steel, so it fades cleanly under a paper overlay.

author: U.S. Department of Energy from United States
why: A researcher watching a culture ferment inside a glass bioreactor vessel: bioprocess engineering at the bench, which is the programme's core.
cropNote: Vessel left of centre, her face right of centre; both survive the 16:10 crop. A top band crops her to eyes-and-glass, still legible. Mostly warm amber and white, fades well.

author: Aisart
why: Fingers holding fine tweezers placing a surface-mount component on a green circuit board: electronics as hands-on assembly.
cropNote: Macro shot, fills any crop. Saturated green is the strongest colour in the set, so it needs the heavier (0.85+) paper overlay; at 0.8 the traces still show through as texture.

author: Aisart
why: Same subject as the SDU Electronics MSc-track record (the BEng is the same discipline): hands placing a component on a circuit board.
cropNote: As dk-sdu-electronics.

author: Peter Seligman
why: An analogue oscilloscope tracing a Lissajous figure on a lab bench, with a trainer panel behind: the measuring side of applied electronics, distinct from the SDU soldering picture.
cropNote: Scope face is centred and survives every crop; the bench is warm wood. Brand name on the scope is small (under 2%).

author: Miha Bukleski
why: Laboratory glassware (funnel, flasks) in sharp foreground on a lab bench, with a scientist in a white coat working further down the room: the teaching lab of the experimental sciences.
cropNote: Soft bokeh background, low contrast: one of the best images in the set for text over a faded picture. Glassware stays readable even as a thin top band.

commonsFile: The Art of the Meal- ZMHS culinary class cooks up feast for Soldiers, community volunteers (9693071).jpg
author: U.S. Army USAGJ by Noriko Kudo
why: Culinary students in whites at work in a teaching kitchen, one chopping at the pass: hospitality training as practice.
cropNote: Chef left of centre survives the crop; bright window light behind keeps it pale and warm. A band crops heads at the chin, so prefer the faded-background treatment.

author: Flexagoon
why: A participant in a 64-channel EEG cap sitting at a screen during an experiment: cognitive science as it is actually done in the lab.
cropNote: Cap and screen sit left and right of centre, both kept by the 16:10 crop; warm beige desk and wall. As a thin band it becomes mostly electrodes, still readable.

author: Eric Kilby
why: A laden container ship alongside ship-to-shore gantry cranes at dusk: the physical side of shipping and trade the programme is about.
cropNote: Ship and cranes sit in the middle third as a dark silhouette against a warm orange sky and flat water; no hull lettering is legible. Very calm for a faded background; as a band it keeps the cranes.

author: Sbaletsk
why: A researcher in a cleanroom suit bent over a probe station with instruments: applied physics and device work, the lab core of Advanced Technology.
cropNote: Figure right of centre, instruments left; the crop keeps both. Almost all white and grey, the easiest kind of image to fade to paper.

author: René Volfík
why: A researcher at a spinning-disk confocal super-resolution microscope, with fluorescent cell images on the monitors: quantitative, instrument-heavy biology at the nanoscale.
cropNote: Microscope left, screens centre, researcher right; the crop keeps all three. The coloured cell images are small patches on a pale lab; fades well, though the monitors stay the brightest element.

author: Mike Reyher
why: Technicians at their stations in a network operations centre: monitoring and defending networks is the day-to-day work the programme trains for.
cropNote: Curved desk runs across the lower third, people at screens mid-frame; ceiling and walls are warm beige. A few monitors show indistinct UI, nothing legible. Fades well; as a band it keeps the desk row.

commonsFile: Programmer writing code with Unit Tests.jpg
author: Joonspoon
why: A student at a desktop with source code open in an editor, working at a warm wooden desk: programming as the everyday activity of computing.
cropNote: Screen and student sit centre-left and right; the crop keeps both. Warm beige tones fade to paper cleanly. The manufacturer logo under the screen is about 1% of the frame.

author: Gabriela Cybulska
why: A technician fitting a performer's motion-capture suit and head rig in a bright capture studio: how characters and animation get into games.
cropNote: Two figures centre; wide white studio around them. One of the palest images in the set, ideal behind dark text. A band crops at the shoulders but keeps the markers and rig.

commonsFile: 2024-02-14 Aufhof KRH Akademie mit VR-Brille der Sophienklink Hannover.jpg
author: Bernd Schwabe in Hannover
why: A person wearing a tethered VR headset with headphones against a pale wall: the XR hardware the programme builds for, shown plainly.
cropNote: Centred and symmetrical; the pale wall with faint line drawing fades to paper, and the orange shirt echoes the site's accent. Top band keeps the headset.

author: Kathyasimon
why: A working costume and fashion workroom: dress forms with garments in progress, cutting tables and thread racks under tall windows. Fashion design as made, not as retail.
cropNote: Dress forms fill the centre third; big pale windows at the top. Warm beige tones overall, fades to paper well. No brand names; the forms carry small maker labels (under 1%).

author: Yevheniia Soldatenko
why: A geologist crouched on a quarry floor measuring a rock slab with a tape: hands-on reading of the subsurface, beside a pool of groundwater. Replaces an earlier hammer-on-strata pick because it shows a person doing the work.
cropNote: Figure and tape sit in the centre; grey shale and green water around them are low in contrast and fade well. A band crops her at the waist but keeps the measuring hand.

commonsFile: A worker ties together reinforcing bar, or rebar, to strengthen concrete floors for a facility that will house 372 students as part of the Herat University Women's Dormitory Project in Herat province 140311-A-DT641-242.jpg
author: Bill Dowell
why: Gloved hands tying reinforcing bar with pliers on a floor slab before the pour: the building technician's trade, close up.
cropNote: Diagonal rebar grid fills the frame; grey concrete and steel with yellow gloves as the one accent. Grid texture is fine and low contrast once faded. The worker is cropped to hands, so no face and no site signage.

commonsFile: Lecture of Igor Masten at the Faculty of Economics in Skopje 06.06.2013 (3).JPG
author: Sazdo
why: An economics lecturer in front of a projected slide of vector error-correction equations: the quantitative, model-driven core of an economics degree (econometrics), not a trading floor or a stock chart.
cropNote: Screen and lecturer sit centre; walls are pale grey, the equations become faint texture once faded. Audience heads are a thin dark strip at the bottom edge, which a 16:10 crop keeps but a paper overlay hides.

commonsFile: The flow of operations at Lakenheath’s wastewater treatment plant (8529232).jpg
author: U.S. Air Force photo by Airman 1st Class Seleena Muhammad-Ali
why: A wastewater operator treating the filter beds at a treatment works, with clarifiers behind: the utility side of water supply and treatment the programme is built around.
cropNote: Operator left of centre, works and trees across the middle band, blue sky above. Warm sunny tones; the sky is the brightest area and sits under the lightest part of the overlay. Band keeps the plant skyline.

author: UCT MOOCs
why: Three people mapping a process on a whiteboard wall of sticky notes: the case-work and teamwork of a business degree, not a boardroom handshake or a skyline.
cropNote: Figures fill the centre and lower half; white wall and scattered coloured notes above. One of the palest images in the set; fades to paper with the notes as small colour flecks. Source is 1280 px wide, so it stores at 1280.

commonsFile: Water supply and sanitation focus groups discussion (7642934958).jpg
author: SuSanA Secretariat
why: A facilitator with a lanyard and notes leading a focus-group discussion, participants seated around her: the qualitative fieldwork method at the heart of the social sciences.
cropNote: People fill the frame edge to edge; teal wall and window grille above. Mid-contrast, so it wants the full paper overlay; faces stay recognisable but soft. Top band crops to the facilitator and the back row.

author: UC Davis College of Engineering
why: Two engineering students in safety glasses assembling machined metal gyroscope tops at a workshop bench, finished pieces in front of them: making and testing a part, which is what an engineering degree does.
cropNote: Students centre-left and centre, bench and parts in the lower third; cream walls behind. Warm and mid-contrast, fades well. Band crops them at the eyes but keeps hands and parts.

author: NASA Kennedy Space Center / NASA/Ben Smegelsky
why: Two technicians in safety glasses setting up a cut on a manual milling machine in a prototype workshop: machining parts is the hands-on base of mechanical engineering.
cropNote: Milling head right of centre, both faces left of centre; all survive the crop. The busiest candidate kept: dark machine body and a red tool chest at the edge, so use the heavier overlay. A small NASA logo on a T-shirt is about 1% of the frame.

author: NASA Kennedy Space Center / NASA/Ben Smegelsky
why: Same discipline as the SDU Mechanical Engineering record: machinists setting up a milling cut.
cropNote: As dk-sdu-mechanical-engineering.

author: NASA Kennedy Space Center / NASA/Ben Smegelsky
why: Same discipline (product development and mechanical design): prototype parts being machined on a mill.
cropNote: As dk-sdu-mechanical-engineering.

author: Σ64
why: The nacelle and hub of a wind turbine seen close up against a pale sky: wind power, the signature field of Danish energy engineering.
cropNote: Nacelle and hub centre-right with blade roots crossing the frame; otherwise near-white sky. The quietest image in the set, so it can take a lighter overlay (0.7). No manufacturer name is visible on this side of the nacelle.

commonsFile: NYC Public Library Research Room Jan 2006-1- 3.jpg
author: Diliff
why: Readers working at long tables in a great research reading room with books and lamps: the reading, source-work and writing that humanities study consists of.
cropNote: Symmetrical: central aisle, readers at tables left and right, arched windows above. Warm wood and cream stone; readers are small, so no faces dominate. The ornate ceiling is the busiest band and sits at the top, where the overlay is lightest, so watch it in the band crop.

author: Lauri Veerde
why: Students wiring and testing a modular automation line (conveyors, pneumatics, a small robot cell and PLC panels) in a mechatronics lab: mechanics, electronics and control in one bench.
cropNote: Stitched wide-angle view, so the edges bow slightly; the students and line sit in the centre. Pale floor and walls; fades cleanly. No readable signage.

author: Lauri Veerde
why: Students wiring and testing a modular automation line (conveyors, pneumatics, a small robot cell and PLC panels) in a mechatronics lab: mechanics, electronics and control in one bench.
cropNote: Stitched wide-angle view, so the edges bow slightly; the students and line sit in the centre. Pale floor and walls; fades cleanly. No readable signage.

author: Zuko.io Images
why: A designer's hands sketching a mobile-screen wireframe on paper while checking a phone: UX and interface design as the planning work behind web and app front-ends.
cropNote: Hands and sketch fill the centre; pale desk and grey jumper. Very calm, one of the best for dark text over a faded image. The phone is unbranded from this angle.

author: Zuko.io Images
why: A designer's hands sketching a mobile-screen wireframe on paper while checking a phone: UX and interface design as the planning work behind web and app front-ends.
cropNote: Hands and sketch fill the centre; pale desk and grey jumper. Very calm, one of the best for dark text over a faded image. The phone is unbranded from this angle.

author: Luka Peternel
why: A researcher and a collaborative robot arm sawing a block of wood together, the robot holding the other end of the saw: robot systems and automation working alongside people.
cropNote: Person left, orange robot arm right, both inside the crop; plain white wall behind. Pale and calm, and the orange arm echoes the site's burnt-orange accent. Band keeps both hands on the saw.

commonsFile: Penciling on Wacom Cintiq 13HD by David Revoy.jpg
author: David Revoy
why: A comic artist's hand pencilling a page of panels on a pen display, for an episode of the webcomic Pepper&Carrot: comics and storyboarding as a working craft.
cropNote: Hand and panels run diagonally through the centre; keyboard top-left. Pencil greys on a pale screen plus a warm wooden desk. Mid-contrast: the black tablet bezel is the darkest mass, lower-left, so use the full overlay behind text.

author: Alexander Baranov from Montpellier, France
why: A hand laying down ink with a brush on a long studio table of work in progress, paint pots and palettes around it, during a painting master class: making art as studio practice.
cropNote: Brush and hand centre-left; white paper fills most of the frame, with black strokes and red blossom as the only strong marks. Very pale, fades cleanly. Shows visual art only; music is not depicted (see README).

author: Vivien Lulkowski/Blender Foundation
why: Pencil pose and expression sketches of a character for the Blender Studio short film Sprite Fright: the drawn acting and pose work at the centre of character animation.
cropNote: Line drawings on a flat grey ground, no people. The crop keeps four poses. Pale and low-contrast, one of the easiest images to put text over. Source is 1288 px wide, so it stores at 1288.

author: Blender Foundation
why: A finished 3D-rendered character in a lit forest set from the Blender Studio short film Sprite Fright: what CG art, 3D modelling and look development produce.
cropNote: Character centre, tree and forest floor around it; warm greens and ambers suit the paper palette. Mid-contrast, so use the full overlay. Band keeps the character's head and the raised prop.

commonsFile: Ennis - Old Ground Hotel - Reception Desk in Lobby - geograph.org.uk - 3052824.jpg
author: Joseph Mischyshyn
why: A receptionist at work behind the panelled front desk of a hotel lobby: front-office operations, the service core of hotel management.
cropNote: Desk runs across the centre with the receptionist small behind it; cream walls and warm wood above. The portrait and red curtain sit top-centre in the lightly faded zone; calm overall. Band keeps the desk and lamps.

author: U.S. Army photo by Hannah Mitchell
why: Site engineers and contractor staff in hard hats and hi-vis inspecting reinforcement and formwork for a new building: construction management as practised on site.
cropNote: Group left of centre walking toward camera; rebar wall recedes to the right, earth and green bank behind. Mid-contrast, needs the full overlay. The vests carry small agency marks (about 1%). Construction is the subject here, not background clutter.

author: U.S. Army photo by Hannah Mitchell
why: Site engineers and contractor staff in hard hats and hi-vis inspecting reinforcement and formwork for a new building: construction management as practised on site.
cropNote: Group left of centre walking toward camera; rebar wall recedes to the right, earth and green bank behind. Mid-contrast, needs the full overlay. The vests carry small agency marks (about 1%). Construction is the subject here, not background clutter.

author: EmilioEsc07
why: A student probing a breadboard circuit with a multimeter at a lab bench: building and testing an electronic prototype, the making side of Creative Technology.
cropNote: Student right, breadboard and meter lower-centre; bright tiled lab around. Pale, warm and calm. Band crops to hands and breadboard, still clear.

author: Army Medicine
why: A veterinarian examining a small dog's eye with an ophthalmoscope while an assistant holds it: clinical veterinary work, close up.
cropNote: Two faces and the dog fill the centre; pale clinic wall behind. Warm skin and teal scrubs; fades softly. Band keeps the scope and the dog's face. The assistant's plain tan T-shirt is the only military trace; there is no insignia in frame.

author: USDA NRCS Montana
why: A soil scientist kneeling in a young crop field with a spade, checking a soil sample: agricultural and environmental science in the field.
cropNote: Figure left of centre, crop rows run diagonally to the horizon, pale sky above. Mostly soft green and beige, fades well. His cap carries a small badge (under 1%).

author: ELSA International from Belgium
why: A law student arguing before the bench in a moot court round, hands mid-gesture, microphone and notes in front: advocacy, the practice at the heart of a law degree.
cropNote: Speaker centre; white curtains behind, so the frame is pale. His name plate and a small competition sign sit at the bottom edge, under the text zone and hidden by the overlay. This is a competition round, but the subject is the argument, not the event.

commonsFile: CMAP - Centre de Mathématiques Appliquées de l'Ecole polytechnique.jpg
author: Jérémy Barande
why: A mathematician working through a probability proof (a Galton-Watson generating function) on a green chalkboard: mathematics as it is done, by hand.
cropNote: Figure centre-bottom, chalk equations fill the upper two-thirds. The green board is darker than most images here, so use the full overlay in light mode; in dark mode it is ideal. Source is 1536 px wide.

commonsFile: A medical student performs eye examination.jpg
author: Sushil Dawka
why: A medical student practising an eye examination with an ophthalmoscope on a clinical training manikin: clinical skills training, the hands-on core of medical school.
cropNote: Student right, manikin head left of centre; pale grey-white room. Very calm, fades cleanly; the student's watch and the manikin's dark torso are the only dark areas, at the bottom left. Source is 1944 px.

author: Hodge120
why: A health worker in a white coat sitting with a patient and taking notes during a clinic consultation: patient-facing health care.
cropNote: Both figures fill the centre; warm wood door left, blue wall right. The blue is the one strong colour and sits in the right third; use the full overlay. Band keeps her face and the patient's shoulder.

commonsFile: Connecting People to Their Public Lands (22957582590).jpg
author: mypubliclands
why: Schoolchildren leaning over a tank of fish from a nearby creek and drawing them in an outdoor lesson: learning by observation, what teacher education prepares people to run.
cropNote: Tank centre-left, children around it; bright, mixed colours (green cap, pink jacket), so it is one of the busier fallbacks and wants the full overlay. Kept because the Commons classroom files are dominated by official visits, ceremonies and paintings.

author: Johan Kosta
why: Two people at a table practising lock picking with tension wrenches and picks: physical security and the attacker's mindset that security-culture teaching starts from. Chosen so Zealand does not repeat Dania's operations-centre picture.
cropNote: Hands and lock sit in the upper-centre, heads frame it; pale wooden table fills the lower half, a clean ground for text. Taken at a lock-picking session at a conference, but the frame shows only the hands-on activity: no banners, stage or signage. The red lanyard is the one strong colour.

author: Lazar.zenit
why: A glass Vigreux distillation column clamped on a lab rig, with a chemist in a white coat out of focus behind: separation processes, the unit operation at the heart of chemical engineering.
cropNote: Column is a vertical stripe left of centre; the rest is soft white and pale-blue bokeh. Among the quietest images in the set. A thin band crops it to glass texture, which still reads as a lab.

author: Blossom Ozurumba
why: Two conference interpreters at work in a booth, headphones on and microphone live: languages as a professional skill, not a flag or a dictionary.
cropNote: Faces upper centre-right, desk and mic lower-left; the pink embroidered blouse is the strongest colour and sits right of centre. Mid-contrast, so use the full overlay. The headphone brand is a tiny mark (under 1%).

commonsFile: U.S. Army Spc. Alejandra Herrera, left, a mechanic with the 7th Squadron, 10th Cavalry Regiment, 1st Brigade Combat Team, 4th Infantry Division, runs on a treadmill during the VO2 Max competition, which 130306-A-UK001-036.jpg
author: Cpl. William Smith
why: An athlete running a VO2-max test on a treadmill in a breathing mask while a tester logs the data: exercise physiology, the science side of a sport degree.
cropNote: Runner left, tester centre, treadmill console right; warm beige gym. The runner's head is at the top-left edge, so a thin band loses it; prefer the faded-background treatment. Treadmill brand text is small (about 1%). Taken at a base fitness event; the frame shows only the test.

author: NSaad (WMF)
why: Students round a table in a small-group tutorial, notes and a laptop between them: the seminar and problem-based discussion that liberal-arts and interdisciplinary programmes are built on.
cropNote: Table runs diagonally through the centre; warm wood and white shirts. The laptop, lower right, is the one dark block and sits under the overlay.
